SMTO-CFG-0090 — SMTO needs your OK to turn on a Skill for this conversation

GUID: 44da9861-3c96-5930-ad11-676aa5646949
Slug: capability-activation-grant-required
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • The agent wants to use a Skill (an add-on set of tools) that is switched off for this conversation. The task is paused until you answer the question it shows.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find the question under the task that asks whether to enable the Skill. Select Allow for this conversation to let SMTO use it, or Don't allow to carry on without it. The Skill is off in this conversation's settings, so only your answer can turn it on for this task.
  2. If SMTO later asks you to approve a specific action or to sign in, answer that request too. Allowing the Skill only makes its tools available; risky actions and account sign-ins are still checked separately.
  3. For next time, select Capabilities in the message box controls, set Apply to to This conversation or Global, set the Skill to Auto, and select Apply. New requests can then pick the Skill straight away, while tasks already running keep the settings they started with.

What success looks like

  • The question disappears and the task continues, using the Skill if you allowed it or other tools if you didn't.

If it still fails

  • If you can't find the question, reload the page. If it still doesn't appear, open Technical details in this panel, select Copy error details, and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Only allow the Skill if you want SMTO to use it; don't allow it just to clear the message.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Capability activation was blocked because the requested Skill is outside the conversation's capability policy but grantable, so the runtime opened a conversation-scoped grant request (grant_request_id) and set the run to waiting_user.

What this means

  • A blocked but prospectively grantable activation needs an explicit conversation capability-policy grant and returns its durable grant_request_id. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • A blocked but prospectively grantable activation needs an explicit conversation capability-policy grant and returns its durable grant_request_id.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact current grant ID, requested Skills and scope; operation permission and credentials remain separate.

How to fix it

  • Answer the open capability_grant interaction with an explicit allow or deny decision bound to its grant_request_id and operation_id (the UI's Allow for this conversation / Don't allow options). Approval adds the Skill to the conversation capability policy and starts a continuation run; operation permissions, unsafe-action checks and credentials are still enforced separately.
  • Ask the user whether to enable this capability for the conversation. Operation permissions and credentials still apply.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended user decision is committed through the matching grant boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
